touches.text: Every answer or reading written here ends with a by-line naming who made the call: "-amm" for Akien's (his initials; he adds it himself to every line he approves), "- <session name>" for a CC session's (eg "- akiendelllinux_orchestrator", "- akienasus_cc_0"). A line without "-amm" is not his call: at most a CC reading, even where it stands in the outline. He says so explicitly when he leaves a call to CC. When an adjudication meets conflicting lines, the by-line is checked first, and "-amm" outranks a CC by-line. Lines written before 2026-11-14 carry none yet. WHY: the by-line says at a glance whose call a line is, so an adjudication starts from who decided rather than re-deriving it. -amm
Trouble Ticket: an error that needs a non-automated fixer (CC or Akien).
Trouble tickets (3.4.3) live here. Any device has a direct line to raise one, not over the bus (2.3.7.1.3).

artifact: the one door a record of truth changes through, and the journal of who came through it (hash-chained, caller read from the kernel). WHY: errors are permanent in records of truth (Law 7), and the journal is what shows a record moved by hand. USERS: everyone who writes a record.

The one writer question is LLM or code (Akien 2026-10-28: "there is no point in tracking the 'authoring entity' ... Whether the write came from an LLM or from deterministic code is really the only question", and only for gate-pass certificates). So on Windows the caller class comes from the process chain: claude.exe above the writer means cc; otherwise it is not cc. Env vars are a fallback only. Certificates are made where the sealer runs (9.4.2.3.3.1), so Windows does not need a gate class of its own. CC's decision, 2026-11-13, on Q#91 (3 teeth of test_artifact_door.py UNRAN on Windows, measured 2026-11-12).

question: the open-question door: a decision only the operator can make, bound to its ticket, answered in the operator's words. WHY: a spec choice is settled by Akien's head, recorded verbatim, never by a paragraph of CC's. USERS: tickets and CodeMother open them; the operator answers (7.4.2).
